questions.question: You need to load 800,000 new Lead records overnight into Salesforce. Which API is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Bulk API 2.0 processes large volumes asynchronously in chunks, avoiding the timeouts and heavy limit consumption a REST loop would hit.

questions.question: Which API would you reach for to deploy a new custom field and Apex class from a CI/CD pipeline?
questions.explanation: Metadata/Tooling APIs manage org configuration (fields, objects, Apex) — exactly what CI/CD deploy tooling uses, unlike the data-focused REST/Bulk APIs.

questions.question: Why pin a specific API version (e.g. v61.0) in a production integration instead of always using the latest?
options: So a future Salesforce release can't silently change behavior under the integration
Pinning a version is required by Salesforce for every callout
It has no real effect, it's just convention
questions.explanation: Salesforce supports many API versions concurrently; pinning protects the integration from unannounced behavior changes in newer versions.

questions.question: What's the main difference between Streaming/Pub-Sub API and REST API for a subscriber that needs continuous updates?
options: Streaming/Pub-Sub pushes events to subscribers in near real time, instead of the subscriber repeatedly polling
Streaming API is only for file uploads
REST API pushes events automatically too
questions.explanation: Streaming/Pub-Sub is a publish-subscribe model; using REST for continuous updates means reintroducing polling, which defeats the purpose.

questions.question: Your integration only needs to read and update a handful of Account records one at a time from a web app. Which API is the simplest default?
questions.explanation: REST API is the lightweight default for general-purpose record CRUD; Bulk API is overkill for small, interactive operations.
